title: Rounding Grades for the Deposit That Restores a Certificate of Deposit
content:
The figure at which a restoring deposit on a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line comes to rest is graded by whether the term has already taken an add-on and by how long the owner has banked with Piedmont Crescent Bank.

## 1. The grades

The rounding of the deposit is graded: where the certificate has taken no add-on since the term began and the owner has held their checking account with the bank for more than 10 years, the deposit is rounded up to the next whole dollar; where the certificate has taken no add-on since the term began and the owner has held their checking account with the bank for 10 years or less, the deposit is rounded down to the whole dollar; otherwise the deposit is rounded to the nearest cent with a half rounded up.

## 2. What is read

The add-ons counted are those taken on the certificate since the term began. The years counted are those the owner's active checking account on the bank's Personal Checking line has been held, from the day it was opened to the day of the deposit. Exactly 10 years falls to the second grade, that grade taking 10 years or less.

## 3. Condition and result

| Add-ons taken since the term began | Years the checking account has been held | The deposit settles |
|---|---|---|
| none | more than 10 | rounded up to the next whole dollar |
| none | 10 or less | rounded down to the whole dollar |
| one or more | more than 10 | rounded to the nearest cent, a half rounded up |
| one or more | 10 or less | rounded to the nearest cent, a half rounded up |

## 4. What the three grades do to one figure

| Figure worked out | Rounded up to the next whole dollar | Rounded down to the whole dollar | Nearest cent, a half rounded up |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8500.40 USD | 8501.00 | 8500.00 | 8500.40 |
| 8500.50 USD | 8501.00 | 8500.00 | 8500.50 |
| 8500.004 USD | 8501.00 | 8500.00 | 8500.00 |
| 8500.00 USD | 8500.00 | 8500.00 | 8500.00 |

A figure already whole in dollars settles at itself under the first two grades; it is not lifted a further dollar.

## 5. Basis Q&A

**Does the length of the relationship matter where the term has already taken an add-on?** No. Both of the first two grades ask first that no add-on has been taken since the term began; where one has, the third grade governs whatever the length of the relationship.
